name: addpipe16_sklansky
rationale: Six prior hand-built adders (Kogge-Stone, conditional-sum, CLA4, two carry-select variants, flat-SOP CLA) all underperformed the plain-'+' baseline, but none has tried a genuine Sklansky-style prefix tree, which differs structurally from Kogge-Stone: instead of updating nearly every bit at every stage with a variable-distance neighbor (49 merge cells total for KS), Sklansky only updates the upper half of each doubling block, merging it with the single boundary result of the lower half (32 merge cells total, ~35% fewer prefix cells than KS at the same log2(16)=4-stage depth). This trades higher fan-out at the final stage's boundary source for substantially reduced total prefix-cell area, which the previous KS attempt (359.366 area, 7.55092 WNS) suggests is close to competitive already; the extra fanout typically gets buffered efficiently by OpenROAD's placer/CTS-like optimization since it appears only once per stage rather than pervasively. This is a structurally distinct point from all six previous attempts and could plausibly land at lower area with comparable WNS to (16,), improving proxy_reward_v0 or establishing a new non-dominated frontier point.
